source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Muhammed,

Thank you for your quick response. We are in the process of submitting a financial model to the government for a potential PPP project. A key requirement is to clearly demonstrate and justify the need for availability-style payments to ensure the project is viable and bankable.

I have attached the Excel template along with additional project details for your review. Please let me know if you are able to support us in developing this model. There might be some errors, please help us check it and make it look professional and clear and strong

value_updates.required_demonstration: Clearly demonstrate and justify the need for availability-style payments

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Please confirm on the following points : 
1. Site list conflict
Your Demand Analysis report and your Business Case use two different 8-site networks (Demand Analysis includes Bowden-Lacombe, Wetaskiwin-Ponoka, Bassano, and Atmore & the Business Case includes Red Deer, Fort McMurray-Suncor, and Medicine Hat instead). Which site list should we treat as final for the financial model the Business Case list, since it has the capital allocation figures?

2. Opex figure conflict
Your original brief states steady-state operating costs of CAD 30-40M/year for the 8-site network, but the Business Case Appendix 1 states annual O&M of only CAD 2.8-3.9M/year a roughly 9x difference. Can you confirm which figure (or cost basis) should be used for the financial model's operating cost assumption?

3. Availability payment sizing target
Should the availability payment be sized only to reach a target minimum DSCR (currently 1.35x), or should it also be sized to deliver a minimum equity IRR (the Business Case cites a 12-18% target range for infrastructure equity)? Under the current DSCR-only approach, equity IRR still comes out negative even after adding the availability payment.

4. Programwide/shared costs
The Business Case's $155M Reference Case includes $11.6M for programwide shared costs (digital platform, program management) plus a $9M reserve/9th-site allowance, on top of the $134.5M in site-level capex. Should we add these as separate line items in the model, or are they excluded from the 8-site financial model scope?

5. Financing terms confirmation
The Business Case describes senior debt at 60-75% of capital, priced at 200-300bps over Government of Canada bond yields, plus optional mezzanine debt. We've modeled a simplified 70/30 debt/equity split at 6% flat. Do you want us to reflect the mezzanine layer separately, or is the simplified single-tranche structure acceptable for this stage?

6. Tax/depreciation
We've applied a flat 25% tax on EBITDA with no depreciation shield modeled yet. Is that acceptable for this stage, or do you need depreciation/CCA (Capital Cost Allowance) reflected given this is a real submission to government?

execution.observed_behavior: Under the current DSCR-only availability-payment approach, modeled equity IRR remains negative even after the payment is added.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
1\. Site list
Use the Business Case site list for the model.

2\. Opex figures
Use the CAD 30–40M/year range from the original brief as the correct program-level operating assumption. The Appendix figure appears understated/incomplete and should not be used for the full network model.

3\. Availability payment approach
Please size the availability payment to achieve both:

\- Minimum DSCR of ~1.35x, and

\-bA minimum equity IRR in the 12–15% range. The model should not rely on DSCR alone if it results in negative equity returns.

4\. Program-wide/shared costs
Include these as separate line items in the model (digital platform, program management, contingency/reserve). They should be treated as part of total program capex, not excluded.

5\. Financing structure
The simplified 70/30 debt/equity at ~6% is acceptable for this stage. No need to layer in mezzanine yet—keep it streamlined and we can refine once we engage lenders.

6\. Tax/depreciation
Please model CCA/depreciation properly using standard Canadian Capital Cost Allowance classes for the relevant asset types (e.g., Class 1 for buildings, Class 43 for clean energy equipment, Class 8 for furniture/fixtures, etc. as applicable). This is essential for a credible government submission and will materially affect the tax shield and equity returns.

The priority is to get to a coherent base-case model quickly, and then iterate

value_updates.sizing_basis: Size the availability payment to achieve both the debt-service and equity-return targets rather than relying on DSCR alone

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Sure that's fine, we can end the contract here.

To be clear on the record the first draft was delivered on time and covered everything in the original brief. When you gave feedback that it was hard to follow, I did not ignore it I delivered a second, substantially revised version addressing that feedback directly. A simplified dashboard, clearly sourced assumptions, separated cash flows for both funding scenarios, additional financial statements, and a short summary presentation for easier review. That second deliverable was sent before you requested this refund, and I did not receive any specific review comments on it, or on the first draft, despite asking.

Given that both milestones were completed and delivered as scoped, I won't be issuing a refund. I'll be raising this through Upwork's dispute process to resolve the remaining milestone payment. You're welcome to leave whatever review you feel is accurate I'll do the same, and I'll let the delivered work and message history speak for themselves.

Happy to end this professionally on both sides.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports that the revised model separates cash flows for both funding scenarios.
